jurisdiction.name: Burkina Faso
jurisdiction.overview: Nationally published records appear separately from applicable EU-level records. The landscape, historical relationships and legal applicability remain under document-level review.

narrative.summary: Burkina Faso's AI governance rests on explicit AI clauses in its 2021 personal data protection law (Law 001-2021/AN), which requires transparency of AI-based processing, prior authorisation by the data protection commission (CIL) for predictive AI decision-support systems and limits on automated decisions. A national AI roadmap to 2030 was validated in June 2026 but has not been published, and there is no AI-specific law. The digital transition ministry's website could not be accessed during this review.
lead_institutions: Commission de l'Informatique et des Libertés (CIL)
narrative.review_notes: This review was carried out on 12 October 2026, but the digital ministry's website and the official gazette search could not be accessed, so only one document could be read. The national AI roadmap is listed as a lead. Burkina Faso is marked for a later retry and, as a country of over 20 million people with few records, for a longer catch-up pass.

instruments.official_title: Loi n°001-2021/AN du 30 mars 2021 portant protection des personnes à l'égard du traitement des données à caractère personnel
instruments.english_title: Law No. 001-2021/AN of 30 March 2021 on the protection of persons with regard to the processing of personal data
instruments.summary: Burkina Faso's general personal data protection law, applying to automated and non-automated processing by public and private controllers established in or operating from the country, with the Commission de l'informatique et des libertés (CIL) as supervisory authority; it repeals Law 010-2004/AN. It contains explicit AI provisions: art. 15 bars court decisions based on automated profiling and administrative or private decisions based solely on it, art. 19 gives a right to know and contest the reasoning of automated processing and, where processing 'relève de l'intelligence artificielle', requires the criteria and nature of the data to be disclosed at collection, and art. 31 makes decision-support processing relying on AI techniques for predictive purposes subject to prior CIL authorisation.
instruments.ai_governance_relevance: General law with explicit AI provisions (transparency of AI-based processing, prior authorisation of predictive AI decision-support, limits on automated decisions).
instruments.current_status: In force. Adopted by the National Assembly in public session on 30 March 2021 (date in the title and the National Assembly PDF); promulgated by Décret n°2021-0276/PRES of 20 April 2021 (text of the promulgation decree published by the CIL at https://cil.bf/wp-content/uploads/2026/09/Decret-2021-0276-promulguant-la-loi-n°001-2021-du-30-mars-2021-portant-protection-des-personnes-a-legart-du-traitement-des-donnees-a-caratere-personnel.pdf), which orders publication in the Journal officiel du Faso (JO issue reference not located). Implementing rules: Décret n°2022-0514/PRES-TRANS/PM/MJDHRI/MEFP of 18 July 2022 on modalities of application (held as a lead). Art. 81 gives existing processing one year from entry into force to comply; art. 82 repeals Law 010-2004/AN of 20 April 2004.
